artifacts.summary: All 6 plan phases completed: shared Python-channel detection library, lint test coverage, an executed corruption-reproduction fixture, a companion write-time Bash hook with its own test suite, hook registration plus a prose pointer, and a final redeploy with scoped gate verification (full battery deferred to the batch stage).

completion_data.completion_summary: Extended lint-state-writer-boundary.sh (gate 12) to the Python/interpreter re-serialization channel via a new shared predicate library, added a companion write-time Bash hook (validate-no-python-state-write.sh) for the shape a content lint cannot see, and pointed task-lock.md's State-Write Convention at both mechanical enforcers. All new test suites pass (28 + 11 cases) against the redeployed tree, with a negative control proving the cases exercise the new code.

memory_candidates.content: When extending a deploy-time content lint and a write-time PreToolUse hook to share one detection predicate, give them OPPOSITE fail-closed/fail-open polarities on a missing/unsourceable shared library: the lint should fail LOUD (exit 2 / error) since a silently-skipped gate check ships unenforced, while the hook should fail OPEN (exit 0, warn on stderr) since a broken write-time guard must never block every matching tool call in the session. Document this asymmetry explicitly in both files' headers rather than leaving it implicit -- it looks like an inconsistency unless the rationale is stated.

When a test case must enumerate 'every real file matching pattern X' under a directory for a control/regression assertion, use `git grep -l` (or otherwise scope to tracked files) rather than a plain recursive `grep -rl`. A plain grep is gitignore-unaware and will nondeterministically sweep in vendored/generated content (e.g. a bootstrapped local venv's site-packages) that happens to exist in the current environment, making the enumerated set -- and therefore the test's pass/fail outcome -- depend on incidental local state rather than the repository's actual tracked content. This bit in practice: a plain grep found 34 files (24 vendored third-party packages) where git grep found the correct 10.

A new shell script file created via a file-write tool (not `cp`/`touch` from an existing executable sibling) does not inherit the executable bit, and a deploy/sync step that copies files byte-for-byte will carry that missing bit into the deployed tree too. A test harness that directly executes suite files (rather than always invoking `bash <path>`) will then SKIP the new suite silently-but-loudly ('not executable (exec-bit regression?)') rather than running it or erroring hard. Always `chmod +x` a newly-created `scripts/tests/*.sh` (or any directly-executed script) in the source store before its first deploy, and re-run the suite discovery step afterward to confirm the file actually ran rather than trusting a clean exit code alone.
